_help._note: Allowed values + requirements per field (this _help block is ignored by the gate — keep or delete). Run `plumb schema` for the full reference.
_help.task_id: required — ticket/issue/branch id (also the receipt filename)
_help.agent_id: required — which agent or human did the work
_help.intent: required — what + why, plain language — the semantic review reads this
_help.self_modifying: one of: true | false — required — MUST be true if changed_files touch policy.protected_paths; touching one with false is a hard fail; true routes to human review
_help.validation_plan: required — each: { command, reason, required, id?, ci_covered? }
_help.validation_plan[].required: one of: true | false — required — is this check mandatory
_help.validation_plan[].id: optional — optional step id; evidence is matched to it via execution_evidence[].step (robust to a command wording diff)
_help.validation_plan[].ci_covered: one of: true | false — optional — step is corroborated by the ci-evidence gate (real CI run), not manual evidence — may be 'skipped'; also auto-recognized when command matches a policy ci_evidence_checks entry
_help.execution_evidence: required — each: { command, status, output_ref?, skip_reason?, step? }
_help.execution_evidence[].status: one of: passed | failed | skipped — required — required steps must be 'passed' (unless CI-covered); use skip_reason when 'skipped'
_help.execution_evidence[].step: optional — optional id of the validation_plan step this evidence is for (matches validation_plan[].id)
_help.changed_files: required — set by `plumb receipt --write` — don't hand-edit
_help.base_sha: optional — pinned merge-base the diff was computed against — makes gate verification deterministic; set by `plumb receipt --write` — never hand-edit
_help.diff_sha256: required — set by `plumb receipt --write` — never hand-edit (computed from base_sha)
_help.result_summary: required — what changed + how it was verified

intent: Make Plumbline CLI binaries execute reliably when npm or npx launches them through a node_modules/.bin symlink. Node 24 preserves the symlink in process.argv[1] while ESM resolves import.meta.url to the target, so the old string comparison silently skipped main() and returned success without running commands. Canonicalizing both paths preserves import-only behavior while fixing normal package-bin execution.

validation_plan.reason: Type-check the new URL and filesystem path handling plus the exported direct-invocation helper.
Compile sources and rebuild the committed dist/index.js package binary that npm executes.
Run the focused regression through an actual filesystem symlink and prove the schema command produces output instead of silently exiting.
Run the complete compiled test suite under Node 24, including temporary git repositories and the new npm-style symlink regression.
Corroborate the repository-standard full test command on the CI Node version configured by the test check.

execution_evidence.output_ref: tsc --noEmit exited 0 with no type errors
TypeScript compilation and esbuild bundle completed; dist/index.js rebuilt at 300.4kb
1 test passed, 0 failed; schema output was produced through a temporary symlink
334 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped under Node 24

execution_evidence.skip_reason: CI-covered by the required test check on the repository's configured Node version

result_summary: Plumbline now compares canonical real paths when deciding whether its ESM CLI module was invoked directly, so npm/npx node_modules/.bin symlinks execute main() on Node 24 while imports remain side-effect free. Added an end-to-end regression that launches the compiled CLI through a real symlink and rebuilt dist/index.js. Type-check, package build, focused regression, and all 334 compiled tests passed locally; the repository-standard npm test command remains covered by CI.
